Log-behavior of the root sequences of P-recursive sequences

Qing-hu Hou and Zhongjie Li Affiliation: School of Mathematics Tianjin University Tianjin 300072, China qh_hou@tju.edu.cn, lizhongjie@tju.edu.cn
Abstract

In recent years, Sun has proposed numerous conjectures regarding the log-concavity of root sequences {ann}n⩾1\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1}. We establish criteria for the asymptotic log-concavity of {ann}n⩾1\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1} and the asymptotic ratio log-convexity of {ann}n⩾1\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1} for PP-recursive sequences {an}n⩾0\{a_{n}\}_{n\geqslant{0}}. Additionally, by the aid of symbolic computation, we present a systematic approach to determine the explicit integer NN such that the sequence {ann}n⩾N\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant{N}} is log-concave and the sequence {ann}n⩾N\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant N} is ratio log-convex.

Keywords: log-concavity, ratio log-convexity, PP-recursive sequences.

1 Introduction

A sequence {an}n⩾1\{a_{n}\}_{n\geqslant 1} is called log-convex (log-concave, respectively) if the inequality an2⩽an+1​an−1a_{n}^{2}\leqslant a_{n+1}a_{n-1} (an2⩾an+1​an−1a_{n}^{2}\geqslant a_{n+1}a_{n-1}, respectively) holds for all n⩾2n\geqslant 2. For a non-negative sequence {an}n⩾1\{a_{n}\}_{n\geqslant 1}, we define its root sequence as {ann}n⩾1\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1}. Recently, Sun [13, 14] proposed several conjectures regarding the log-concavity of the root sequences of combinatorial sequences. Some of these conjectures have been confirmed, as shown in [5, 10, 12, 17]. In particular, Xia [16] developed a systematic method to prove the log-concavity of {ann}n⩾1\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1} when ana_{n} satisfies a second-order linear reucrrence.

We consider the general case where {an}n⩾1\{a_{n}\}_{n\geqslant 1} is a P-recursive sequence. Recall that a PP-recursive sequence {an}n⩾1\{a_{n}\}_{n\geqslant 1} of order dd satisfies a recurrence relation of the form

p0​(n)​an+p1​(n)​an+1+⋯+pd​(n)​an+d=0,∀n⩾1,p_{0}(n)a_{n}+p_{1}(n)a_{n+1}+\cdots+p_{d}(n)a_{n+d}=0,\quad\forall\,n\geqslant 1,

where pi​(n)p_{i}(n) are polynomials in nn. Wimp and Zeilberger [15] (see also [3, Sec. VIII.7]) showed that a PP-recursive sequence {an}n⩾1\{a_{n}\}_{n\geqslant 1} is asymptotically equal to a linear combination of terms in the form of

eQ⁡(ρ,n)​s​(ρ,n),e^{Q(\rho,n)}s(\rho,n), (1.1)

where

Q⁡(ρ,n)\displaystyle Q(\rho,n) =μ0​n​log⁡n+∑j=1ρμj​nj/ρ,\displaystyle=\mu_{0}n\log{n}+\sum_{j=1}^{\rho}\mu_{j}n^{j/\rho}, (1.2)
s⁡(ρ,n)\displaystyle s(\rho,n) =nr∑j=0t−1(logn)j∑s=0∞bs​jn−s/ρ,\displaystyle=n^{r}\sum_{j=0}^{t-1}(\log{n})^{j}\sum_{s=0}^{\infty}b_{sj}n^{-s/\rho}, (1.3)

with ρ,t\rho,\ t being positive integers and μj,r,bs​j\mu_{j},\ r,\ b_{sj} being complex numbers. We focus on the case where ana_{n} asymptotically takes the form of (1.1) and t=1t=1 in (1.3), which encompasses the majority of combinatorial sequences.

Based on the asymptotic expression of ana_{n}, we establish a criterion for ana_{n} such that the root sequences {ann}\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\} is asymptotically log-concave, i.e.,

ann2⩾an−1n−1​an+1n+1\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}^{2}\geqslant\sqrt[n-1]{a_{n-1}}\sqrt[n+1]{a_{n+1}}

holds for all sufficiently large nn. We define a sequence {an}n⩾1\{a_{n}\}_{n\geqslant 1} to be ratio log-convex if {an+1/an}n⩾1\{a_{n+1}/a_{n}\}_{n\geqslant 1} is log-convex. By a similar discussion, we provide a criterion for ana_{n} such that the root sequence is asymptotically ratio log-convex.

Our next objective is to identify a specific integer NN that guarantees the log-concavity of the sequence {ann}n⩾N\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant N}. We solve the problem by establishing bounds for both rn=an+1/anr_{n}=a_{n+1}/a_{n} and ana_{n}. Notably, Hou and Zhang [6] have developed an algorithm to compute NN and provide bounds for the ratio rnr_{n} when n⩾Nn\geqslant N. Combing with the asymptotic expression of ana_{n}, we are enable to give an upper bound of ana_{n} as intended. Then we can use Maple or Mathematica to find the derivative and limiting value in order to prove the constant positivity or negativity of the rational function.

This paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, by studying the asymptotic expressions of PP-recursive sequences, we give a criterion of the asymptotic log-concavity for the sequence {ann}n⩾1\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1} and the asymptotic ratio log-convexity for {ann}n⩾1\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1}. In Section 3, by studying the log-behavior of {ann}n⩾1\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1} and the monotonicity of {an+1nann}n⩾1\left\{\frac{\sqrt[n]{a_{n+1}}}{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}}\right\}_{n\geqslant 1}, we extend the result of [6] to give a systematic method to find NN such that the sequence {ann}n⩾N\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant{N}} is log-concave and {ann}n⩾N\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant N} is ratio log-convex.

2 The asymptotic log-behavior of {ann}n⩾1\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1}

In this section, we consider that the asymptotic log-concavity and the asymptotic ratio log-convexity.

Firstly, we give a sufficient condition for the log-concavity of {ann}n⩾1.\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1}.

Theorem 2.1.

Suppose that {an}n⩾1\{a_{n}\}_{n\geqslant{1}} is a P-recursive sequence whose asymptotic expression is

an∼eQ⁡(ρ,n)⋅nr(∑s=0Mbsn−s/ρ+o(n−M/ρ)),\displaystyle a_{n}\sim e^{Q(\rho,n)}\cdot n^{r}\left(\sum_{s=0}^{M}b_{s}n^{-s/\rho}+o(n^{-M/\rho})\right), (2.1)

where

Q⁡(ρ,n)=μ0​n​log⁡n+∑j=1ρμj​nj/ρ,Q(\rho,n)=\mu_{0}n\log{n}+\sum_{j=1}^{\rho}\mu_{j}n^{j/\rho},

b0>0andM/ρ>2.b_{0}>0\quad\mbox{and}\quad M/\rho>2.

Then for the following three cases, the sequence {ann}n⩾1\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant{1}} is asymptotically log-concave.

    μ0>0\mu_{0}>{0}.

  • (2)

    μ0=0\mu_{0}=0 and μk<0,\mu_{k}<{0}, where k=max1⩽j⩽ρ−1⁡{j:μj≠0}k=\max\limits_{1\leqslant{j}\leqslant{\rho-1}}\{j\colon\mu_{j}\neq{0}\}.

  • (3)

    μ0=0,μj=0\mu_{0}=0,\ \mu_{j}=0 for 1⩽j⩽ρ−11\leqslant{j}\leqslant{\rho-1}, and r<0r<{0}.

Combining (2.3)–(2.6) together, we arrive at

Δ=\displaystyle\Delta= −μ0n2+∑j=1ρ−1μj​(j/ρ−1)​(j/ρ−2)n3−j/ρ+r⁡(2​log⁡n−3)n3\displaystyle-\frac{\mu_{0}}{n^{2}}+\sum_{j=1}^{\rho-1}\frac{\mu_{j}(j/\rho-1)(j/\rho-2)}{n^{3-j/\rho}}+\frac{r(2\log{n}-3)}{n^{3}}

It is straightforward to see that when the parameters satisfy one of (1)–(3), the coefficient of the dominant term in the asymptotic expression of Δ\Delta is negative. ∎

Remark. We can further discuss the case where μ0=0\mu_{0}=0, μj=0\mu_{j}=0 for 1⩽j⩽ρ−11\leqslant{j}\leqslant{\rho-1}, and r=0r=0. In this case, the asymptotic log-concavity depends on whether b0b_{0} is less than 11. However, determining the explicit value of b0b_{0} is non-trivial since it depends on both the recursion and initial values of the sequence ana_{n}.

Note that when ana_{n} has the asymptotic form (2.1), an/nαa_{n}/n^{\alpha} will have the asymptotic form

an∼eQ⁡(ρ,n)⋅nr−α(∑s=0Mbsn−s/ρ+o(n−M/ρ)).a_{n}\sim e^{Q(\rho,n)}\cdot n^{r-\alpha}\left(\sum_{s=0}^{M}b_{s}n^{-s/\rho}+o(n^{-M/\rho})\right).

Therefore, the above criteria applies to the sequence {an/nαn}n⩾1\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}/n^{\alpha}}\}_{n\geqslant 1} by replacing rr with r−αr-\alpha.

With a similar discussion, we find a criterion which guarantees the asymptotic ratio log-convexity of the root sequence.

Theorem 2.2.

Suppose that {an}n⩾1\{a_{n}\}_{n\geqslant{1}} is a P-recursive sequence whose asymptotic expression is

an∼eQ⁡(ρ,n)⋅nr(∑s=0Mbsn−s/ρ+o(n−M/ρ)),\displaystyle a_{n}\sim e^{Q(\rho,n)}\cdot n^{r}\left(\sum_{s=0}^{M}b_{s}n^{-s/\rho}+o(n^{-M/\rho})\right), (2.8)

where

Q⁡(ρ,n)=μ0​n​log⁡n+∑j=1ρμj​nj/ρ,Q(\rho,n)=\mu_{0}n\log{n}+\sum_{j=1}^{\rho}\mu_{j}n^{j/\rho},

with ρ,M\rho,M being positive integers and μj,r,bs\mu_{j},r,b_{s} being real numbers such that

b0>0andM/ρ>3.b_{0}>0\quad\mbox{and}\quad M/\rho>3.

Then for the following three cases, the sequence {ann}n⩾1\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant{1}} is asymptotically ratio log-convex.

  • (1)

    μ0>0\mu_{0}>{0}.

  • (2)

    μ0=0\mu_{0}=0 and μk<0,\mu_{k}<{0}, where k=max1⩽j⩽ρ−1⁡{j:μj≠0}k=\max\limits_{1\leqslant{j}\leqslant{\rho-1}}\{j\colon\mu_{j}\neq{0}\}.

  • (3)

    μ0=0,μj=0\mu_{0}=0,\ \mu_{j}=0 for 1⩽j⩽ρ−11\leqslant{j}\leqslant{\rho-1}, and r<0r<{0}.

Proof.

Notice that

(an+1n+1ann)2⩽an+2n+2an+1n+1⋅annan−1n−1\left(\frac{\sqrt[n+1]{a_{n+1}}}{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}}\right)^{2}\leqslant\frac{\sqrt[n+2]{a_{n+2}}}{\sqrt[n+1]{a_{n+1}}}\cdot\frac{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}}{\sqrt[n-1]{a_{n-1}}}

if and only if

Δ′=−log⁡an+2n+2+3​log⁡an+1n+1−3​log⁡ann+log⁡an−1n−1⩽0.\Delta^{\prime}=-\frac{\log a_{n+2}}{n+2}+3\frac{\log a_{n+1}}{n+1}-3\frac{\log a_{n}}{n}+\frac{\log a_{n-1}}{n-1}\leqslant 0.

By analyzing each factor in the asymptotic expression of ana_{n}, as done in the proof of Theorem 2.1, we derive that

Δ′=\displaystyle\Delta^{\prime}= −2​μ0n3−∑j=1ρ−1μj​(j/ρ−1)​(j/ρ−2)​(j/ρ−3)n4−j/ρ+r⁡(6​log⁡n−11)n4\displaystyle-\frac{2\mu_{0}}{n^{3}}-\sum\limits_{j=1}^{\rho-1}\frac{\mu_{j}(j/\rho-1)(j/\rho-2)(j/\rho-3)}{n^{4-j/\rho}}+\frac{r(6\log n-11)}{n^{4}}
+∑s=0Mb~s​(1+s/ρ)​(2+s/ρ)​(3+s/ρ)n4+s/ρ+⋯+o(1n1+M/ρ).\displaystyle+\sum\limits_{s=0}^{M}\frac{\tilde{b}_{s}(1+s/\rho)(2+s/\rho)(3+s/\rho)}{n^{4+s/\rho}}+\dots+o\left(\frac{1}{n^{1+M/\rho}}\right).

The proof follows immediately. ∎

Example 2.3.

Let GnG_{n} be the number of graphs on [n]={1,…,n}[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\} whose every component is a cycle (see [7, Example 3.7]). We have

Gn+1=(n+1)​Gn−(n2)​Gn−2G_{n+1}=(n+1)G_{n}-\binom{n}{2}G_{n-2}

with initial values G0=1,G1=1,G2=2.G_{0}=1,G_{1}=1,G_{2}=2.

It can be computed by our Mathematica package P-rec.m that

Gn∼C⋅en​log⁡n−n​(1+1124​n+9131152​n2+829543414720​n3+o⁡(1n3)).G_{n}\sim C\cdot e^{n\log n-n}\left(1+\frac{11}{24n}+\frac{913}{1152n^{2}}+\frac{829543}{414720n^{3}}+o\left(\frac{1}{n^{3}}\right)\right).

Since μ0=1>0\mu_{0}=1>0, we immediately derive that the root sequence {Gnn}n⩾1\{\sqrt[n]{G_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1} is asymptotically log-concave and ratio log-convex. Moreover, the sequence {Gn/nαn}n⩾1\{\sqrt[n]{G_{n}/n^{\alpha}}\}_{n\geqslant 1} is asymptotically log-concave for any real number α\alpha.

3 Finding the explicit NN

In this section, we aim to determine a specific value for NN such that {ann}n⩾N\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant{N}} is log-concave or ratio log-convex. In their work [6], Hou and Zhang introduced an algorithm for computing an integer NN along with lower and upper bounds for rn=an+1/anr_{n}=a_{n+1}/a_{n} when n⩾Nn\geqslant N. Our approach relies on these bounds together with an upper bound for ana_{n}. It is worth to note that deriving these bounds for rnr_{n} requires the sequence {an}n⩾1\{a_{n}\}_{n\geqslant 1} to be bound preserving, as defined in [6].

Firstly, we give a criterion on the log-concavity of the root sequences.

Theorem 3.1.

Let {an}n⩾1\{a_{n}\}_{n\geqslant{1}} be a positive sequence. Suppose we can find an upper bound hnh_{n} of ana_{n}, a lower bound fnf_{n} and an upper bound gng_{n} of an+1an\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_{n}}, such that

2​log​hn+n⁡(n+1)​log​gn+1−n⁡(n+3)​log​fn⩽0,∀n⩾N.2\log h_{n}+n(n+1)\log g_{n+1}-n(n+3)\log f_{n}\leqslant 0,\quad\forall n\geqslant N. (3.1)

Then the root sequence {ann}n⩾N\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant{N}} is log-concave.

Proof.

From the definition, the log-concavity of {ann}n⩾N\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant{N}} is equivalent to

log⁡an+2n+2+log⁡ann−2​log⁡an+1n+1⩽0.\dfrac{\log{a_{n+2}}}{n+2}+\dfrac{\log{a_{n}}}{n}-\dfrac{2\log{a_{n+1}}}{n+1}\leqslant{0}. (3.2)

Denote rn=an+1/anr_{n}=a_{n+1}/a_{n}. Substituting an+2=an​rn​rn+1a_{n+2}=a_{n}r_{n}r_{n+1} and an+1=an​rna_{n+1}=a_{n}r_{n} in (3.2), we get an equivalent inequality

2​log​an+n⁡(n+1)​log​rn+1−n⁡(n+3)​log​rn⩽0.2\log a_{n}+n(n+1)\log r_{n+1}-n(n+3)\log r_{n}\leqslant 0.

Notice that

2​log​an+n⁡(n+1)​log​rn+1−n⁡(n+3)​log​rn\displaystyle 2\log a_{n}+n(n+1)\log r_{n+1}-n(n+3)\log r_{n}
⩽\displaystyle\leqslant\ 2​log​hn+n⁡(n+1)​log​gn+1−n⁡(n+3)​log​fn.\displaystyle 2\log h_{n}+n(n+1)\log g_{n+1}-n(n+3)\log f_{n}.

The proof follows immediately. ∎

Remark. Assume that {an}n⩾1\{a_{n}\}_{n\geqslant 1} is a bound preserving sequence. We can use the Mathematica package P-rec.m to compute NN and bounds fn,gnf_{n},\ g_{n} for an+1/ana_{n+1}/a_{n}. By using the command

RootLog[L, n, N, ini_val, K]


where

L=Nd−(R0​(n)+R1​(n)​N+⋯+Rd−1​(n)​Nd−1)L=N^{d}-(R_{0}(n)+R_{1}(n)N+\cdots+R_{d-1}(n)N^{d-1})

corresponds to the recurrence relation

an+d=R0​(n)​an+R1​(n)​an+1+⋯+Rd−1​(n)​an+d−1,a_{n+d}=R_{0}(n)a_{n}+R_{1}(n)a_{n+1}+\cdots+R_{d-1}(n)a_{n+d-1},

ini_val is a list of initial values of the sequences and K is the number of terms of the asymptotic ratio of the sequence. Then we can get

{{fn,gn},N}\{\{f_{n},\ g_{n}\},\ N\}

which indicates that

fn≤an+1/an≤gnf_{n}\leq a_{n+1}/a_{n}\leq g_{n}

for n≥N.n\geq N. And for the three cases in Theorem 2.1, we can always find an upper bound for ana_{n} such that (3.1) holds, implying the log-concavity of the root sequence.

In fact, we may take

hn=eQ⁡(ρ,n)​nr+ϵh_{n}=e^{Q(\rho,n)}n^{r+\epsilon}

for a certain ϵ>0\epsilon>0. On one hand, by aid of the upper bound gng_{n}, we can show that hnh_{n} is really an upper bounds for ana_{n}. On the other hand, from (2.7) we see that the leading term in the asymptotic expression of

2​log​hn+n⁡(n+1)​log​rn+1−n⁡(n+3)​log​rn2\log h_{n}+n(n+1)\log r_{n+1}-n(n+3)\log r_{n}

is negative, which ensures that (3.1) holds when fn,gnf_{n},g_{n} are tight enough.

The following example illustrates the computation.

Example 3.2.

Let

an=fn(5)=∑k=0n(nk)5a_{n}=f_{n}^{(5)}=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\binom{n}{k}^{5}

be the Franel numbers of order 55. The root sequence of {an}n⩾1\{a_{n}\}_{n\geqslant 1} is log-concave.

By [9] or Zeilberger’s algorithm, we find that ana_{n} satisfies the recurrence:

32​(55​n2+33​n+6)​(n−1)4​an−2−(19415​n6−27181​n5+7453​n4+3289​n3−956​n2CLOSEOPEN−276​n+96)​an−1−(1155​n6+693​n5−732​n4−715​n3+45​n2+210​n+56)​an+(55​n2−77​n+28)​(n+1)4​an+1=0,32(55n^{2}+33n+6)(n-1)^{4}a_{n-2}-(19415n^{6}-27181n^{5}+7453n^{4}+3289n^{3}-956n^{2}\\ -276n+96)a_{n-1}-(1155n^{6}+693n^{5}-732n^{4}-715n^{3}+45n^{2}+210n+56)a_{n}\\ +(55n^{2}-77n+28)(n+1)^{4}a_{n+1}=0,

with initial values

f0(5)=1,f1(5)=2,f2(5)=34,f3(5)=488.f_{0}^{(5)}=1,\,f_{1}^{(5)}=2,\,f_{2}^{(5)}=34,\,f_{3}^{(5)}=488.

By using the package P-rec.m, we obtain the asymptotic expansion of ana_{n}

an∼C⋅32n​n−2​(1−45​n+725​n+2125​n3+o⁡(1n3)),a_{n}\sim C\cdot 32^{n}n^{-2}\left(1-\frac{4}{5n}+\frac{7}{25n}+\frac{2}{125n^{3}}+o\left(\frac{1}{n^{3}}\right)\right),

where CC is a certain constant. Furthermore, we obtain bounds for rn=an+1/anr_{n}=a_{n+1}/a_{n}:

fn≤rn≤gn,∀n⩾414,f_{n}\leq r_{n}\leq g_{n},\quad\forall\,n\geqslant{414},

with

fn=32−64n+6035​n2,gn=32−64n+6135​n2.f_{n}=32-\frac{64}{n}+\frac{603}{5n^{2}},\quad g_{n}=32-\frac{64}{n}+\frac{613}{5n^{2}}.

Next, we will show that hn=32n/nh_{n}=32^{n}/n is an upper bound for ana_{n} when n⩾414n\geqslant 414 by induction. Initially, one can check that the inequality holds for n=414n=414. Assume it holds for ana_{n}, i.e., an≤hna_{n}\leq h_{n}. Notice that

an+1=an​rn≤hn​gna_{n+1}=a_{n}r_{n}\leq h_{n}g_{n}

and

hn+1−hn​gnhn=160​n2−293​n−6135​n2​(n+1)>0,∀n⩾4.\frac{h_{n+1}-h_{n}g_{n}}{h_{n}}=\frac{160n^{2}-293n-613}{5n^{2}(n+1)}>0,\quad\forall\,n\geqslant 4.

We thus derive that an+1≤hn+1a_{n+1}\leq h_{n+1}.

Now we will show that

D⁡(n)=2​log​hn+n⁡(n+1)​log​gn+1−n⁡(n+3)​log​fn≤0,n⩾19.D(n)=2\log h_{n}+n(n+1)\log g_{n+1}-n(n+3)\log f_{n}\leq 0,\quad n\geqslant 19.

By Maple, we compute that

limn→+∞D⁡(n)=−∞,limn→+∞D′​(n)=limn→+∞D′′​(n)=0,\lim_{n\to+\infty}D(n)=-\infty,\quad\lim_{n\to+\infty}D^{\prime}(n)=\lim_{n\to+\infty}D^{\prime\prime}(n)=0,

and

By calculating the maximum root of the numerator in the expression for D′′′​(n)D^{\prime\prime\prime}(n), we determine that D′′′​(n)<0D^{\prime\prime\prime}(n)<0 when n⩾19n\geqslant 19. Consequently, D′′​(n)>0D^{\prime\prime}(n)>0 and D′​(n)<0D^{\prime}(n)<0 for n⩾19n\geqslant 19. It is straightforward to check that D⁡(19)<0D(19)<0, implying that D⁡(n)<0D(n)<0 for n⩾19n\geqslant 19. By examining the initial terms, we derive that Dn<0D_{n}<0 for n⩾16n\geqslant 16.

In summary, we have proved that the root sequence of {fn(5)}n⩾414\{f_{n}^{(5)}\}_{n\geqslant 414} is log-concave. By further examination of the initial values, we see that the root sequence of {fn(5)}n⩾1\{f_{n}^{(5)}\}_{n\geqslant{1}} is log-concave, completing the proof.

We have implement a Mathematica package P-rec.m (which is available at [1]) to do the above computations. Utilizing this package, we confirm Conjecture 3.10 in [13] for r=3,4,5r=3,4,5. We also reprove the log-concavity of the root sequences of the following sequences: {Sn}n⩾1\{S_{n}\}_{n\geqslant{1}} in [11], {Rn}n⩾5\{{R_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant{5}} in [10], {an}n⩾2\{{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant{2}} and {bn}n⩾1\{{b_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant{1}} in [17], the Catalan-Larcombe-French sequence {Pn}n⩾1\{{P_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant{1}} in [18], the Zagier numbers {Zn}n⩾1\{{Z_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1}, the Apéry numbers {An}n⩾1\{{A_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1}, the Domb numbers {Dn}n⩾1\{{D_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1}, the Motzkin numbers {Mn}n⩾1\{{M_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1}, the Cohen-Rhin numbers {Un}n⩾1\{{U_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1} in [16], and the sequences in [2] and [8].

Replacing ana_{n} by an/nαa_{n}/n^{\alpha}, we can find the explicit NαN_{\alpha} such that the root sequence of {an/nα}n⩾Nα\{{a_{n}/n^{\alpha}}\}_{n\geqslant N_{\alpha}} is log-concave. Here is an example.

Example 3.3.

Let Cn=(2​nn)/(n+1)C_{n}={2n\choose n}/(n+1) be the Catalan numbers and an=1/Cna_{n}=1/C_{n} (see [4]). Then the root sequence of {an/n2}n⩾6\{{a_{n}/n^{2}}\}_{n\geqslant 6} is log-concave.

Let bn=an/n2b_{n}=a_{n}/n^{2}. It is straightforward to see that

(4​n+2)​(n+1)2​bn+1−n2​(n+2)​bn=0.(4n+2)(n+1)^{2}b_{n+1}-n^{2}(n+2)b_{n}=0.

By the package P-rec.m, we find that

bn∼C⋅n−12​4−n​(1+98​n+17128​n2+31024​n3+o⁡(1n3)),b_{n}\sim C\cdot n^{-\frac{1}{2}}4^{-n}\left(1+\frac{9}{8n}+\frac{17}{128n^{2}}+\frac{3}{1024n^{3}}+o\left(\frac{1}{n^{3}}\right)\right),

for some constant CC. Noting that

rn=bn+1bn=n2​(n+2)2​(2​n+1)​(n+1)2,r_{n}=\frac{b_{n+1}}{b_{n}}=\frac{n^{2}(n+2)}{2(2n+1)(n+1)^{2}},

we may take fn=gn=rnf_{n}=g_{n}=r_{n} as the lower and upper bounds for rnr_{n}. Moreover, for n⩾2n\geqslant 2, we have an upper bound for bnb_{n}:

hn=4−nn1/4.h_{n}=\frac{4^{-n}}{n^{{1}/{4}}}.

This can be shown by noting

limn→+∞D⁡(n)=0,D′​(n)=−2​n2+23​n+144​n​(2​n3+7​n2+7​n+2)<0,\lim_{n\to+\infty}D(n)=0,\quad D^{\prime}(n)=-\frac{2n^{2}+23n+14}{4n(2n^{3}+7n^{2}+7n+2)}<0,

where

D⁡(n)=log⁡(hn+1)−log⁡(gn​hn).D(n)=\log(h_{n+1})-\log(g_{n}h_{n}).

Similarly, we can verify that

D⁡(n)=2​log​hn+n⁡(n+1)​log​gn+1−n⁡(n+3)​log​fn≤0,n⩾26.D(n)=2\log h_{n}+n(n+1)\log g_{n+1}-n(n+3)\log f_{n}\leq 0,\quad n\geqslant 26.

Finally, by checking initial values, we find that {bnn}n⩾20\{\sqrt[n]{b_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 20} is log-concave.

Similar to Theorem 3.1, we can establish a criterion for the ratio log-convexity of the root sequence {ann}n⩾N\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant N}. We will omit the proof as it closely parallels that of Theorem 3.1.

Theorem 3.4.

Let {an}n⩾1\{a_{n}\}_{n\geqslant{1}} be a positive sequence. Suppose we can find an upper bound hnh_{n} of ana_{n}, a lower bound fnf_{n} and an upper bound gng_{n} of an+1an\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_{n}}, such that for n⩾Nn\geqslant N

6​log​hn+(n2−n)​(2​n+5)​log​gn−(n2+n)​(n+2)​log​fn−1−(n3−n)​log​fn+1⩽0.6\log h_{n}+(n^{2}-n)(2n+5)\log g_{n}-(n^{2}+n)(n+2)\log f_{n-1}-(n^{3}-n)\log f_{n+1}\leqslant 0.

Then the root sequence {ann}n⩾N\{\sqrt[n]{a_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant{N}} is ratio log-convex.

We give an example to illustrate the application of Theorem 3.4.

Example 3.5.

Let MnM_{n} be the Motzkin numbers which satisfy

(n+4)​Mn+2−(2​n+5)​Mn+1−3​(n+1)​Mn=0,n⩾0.(n+4)M_{n+2}-(2n+5)M_{n+1}-3(n+1)M_{n}=0,\quad n\geqslant 0.

Then the root sequence {Mnn}n⩾1\{\sqrt[n]{M_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1} is ratio log-convex.

By the package P-rec.m, we find that

Mn∼C⋅3nn−3/2(1−3916​n+2665512​n2−878858192​n3+o(1n3)),M_{n}\sim C\cdot 3^{n}n^{-3/2}\left(1-\frac{39}{16n}+\frac{2665}{512n^{2}}-\frac{87885}{8192n^{3}}+o\left(\frac{1}{n^{3}}\right)\right),

for some constant C.C. Moreover, for n⩾228n\geqslant{228} we have the lower and upper bound of rn=Mn+1/Mnr_{n}=M_{n+1}/M_{n}:

fn=3−92​n+20716​n2−1574​n3,f_{n}=3-\frac{9}{2n}+\frac{207}{16n^{2}}-\frac{157}{4n^{3}},

and

gn=3−92​n+20716​n2−1494​n3.g_{n}=3-\frac{9}{2n}+\frac{207}{16n^{2}}-\frac{149}{4n^{3}}.

Now we take

hn=3nn.h_{n}=\frac{3^{n}}{n}.

It can be verified that for n⩾15,n\geqslant{15},

6​log​hn+(n2−n)​(2​n+5)​log​gn−(n2+n)​(n+2)​log​fn−1−(n3−n)​log​fn+1⩽0.6\log h_{n}+(n^{2}-n)(2n+5)\log g_{n}-(n^{2}+n)(n+2)\log f_{n-1}-(n^{3}-n)\log f_{n+1}\leqslant 0.

Finally, by checking initial values, we derive that {Mnn}n⩾1\{\sqrt[n]{M_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant{1}} is ratio log-convex.

In a similar way, we show that the root sequences of the following combinatorial sequences are all ratio log-convex: Fine numbers {fn}n⩾4\{{f_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 4}, the central Delannoy numbers {Dn}n⩾1\{{D_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1}, the Domb numbers {Dn}n⩾1\{{D_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1}, the numbers of tree-like polyhexes with n+1n+1 hexagons {tn}n⩾1\{{t_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant{1}}, and the Catalan-Larcombe-French sequence {Pn}n⩾1\{{P_{n}}\}_{n\geqslant 1}.
